inventory.name: [NopalCyber] Suspicious ADRS Token Request by Microsoft Auth Broker

properties.description: This rule will identifies Entra ID sign-in events where a user authenticates using a refresh token issued to the Microsoft Authentication Broker (MAB) client, targeting the Device Registration Service (DRS) with the "adrs_access" OAuth scope. This pattern is a strong indicator of an adversary using a stolen refresh token to initiate a malicious device registration flow, often with tools like ROADtx, as a step towards establishing persistence
properties.displayName: [NopalCyber] Suspicious ADRS Token Request by Microsoft Auth Broker
properties.query:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
// Filter for successful sign-ins from member accounts (users).
| where ResultType == 0
| where UserType == "Member"
// The client application is the Microsoft Authentication Broker (MAB).
| where AppId == "29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e"
// The target resource is the Device Registration Service (DRS).
| where ResourceIdentity == "01cb2876-7ebd-4aa4-9cc9-d28bd4d359a9"
// The authentication was performed using a refresh token.
| where IncomingTokenType == "refreshToken"
// The token was specifically scoped for Azure DRS access.
| where AuthenticationProcessingDetails has "adrs_access"
| project-reorder
    TimeGenerated,
    UserPrincipalName,
    AppDisplayName,
    IPAddress,
    Location,
    ResourceDisplayName,
    AuthenticationProcessingDetails,
    DeviceDetail,
    UserAgent,
    CorrelationId
